hypothesis_update: The empty HashSet passed as the third argument to rewrite_statements at compose.rs:318 is a suspected data-integrity defect: component init statements are rewritten with an empty name context, which either (a) leaves component-local references unresolved or (b) incorrectly rewrites names that should be local to the component, producing a silently wrong kernel spec. The asymmetry with rewrite_compose_statements (which receives the full component map) supports this. Secondary hypothesis: the internal set (lines 291–298) used to filter actions is never validated against known component aliases, so an Internal item referencing an unknown alias would silently leave the corresponding action exposed as public rather than returning the CoreError the documented contract promises.
rationale: The target body calls rewrite_statements(statements.clone(), component, &HashSet::new()) at line 318 for every component-level init, passing an empty set as the third argument. This is asymmetric with rewrite_compose_statements(statements.clone(), &components) at line 345, which takes no such set. Without seeing the definition of rewrite_statements (lines 585–740), it is impossible to determine what the third parameter represents — whether it is a visibility scope, a set of already-resolved names, or a set of names to skip — and therefore whether the empty set is correct or a data-integrity bug that would cause init statements to be rewritten against the wrong name environment, silently producing an incorrect kernel.
